simple.meaning: סִיג (çîyg) is a Hebrew object word meaning “scoria.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

firstOccurrence.englishText: You put away all the wicked of the earth like dross.

timeline.evidenceText: You put away all the wicked of the earth like dross.
Take away the dross from the silver,

I will turn my hand on you,

definitions.full: H5509. sig or sug שִׂיג סִיג, noun [masculine] 1 a moving back or away ; 2 dross ( what is removed from metal); — absolute סִיג Ezek 22:18 Qr ( סוג Kt), שִׂיג 1Kin 18:27 **omitted ᵐ5 L, dittograph for שִׂיחַ Klo Bur. ( שׂ for ס , but see below); plural סִיגִים (van d. H. סִגִּים ) Isa 1:22 3 t.; סִגִֿים Ezek 22:18 2 t.; suffix סִיגָ֑יִךָ Isa 1:25 ; — 1 a moving back, away: לוֺ שִׂיג 1Kin 18:27 there is a moving back to him = he has moved back, away (probably of temporary withdrawal, different from דֶּרֶךְ journey ). 2 dross , usually of silver Prov 25:4 ( מִכָּ֑סֶף ), 26:23 ס ׅ׳(כֶּסֶף , so (figurative of Israel) Isa 1:22 compare see 25, Ezek 22:18 b ( ᵐ5 ׳כ ׳ס בְּתוֺךְ ᵑ0, כֶּסֶף סִיגִים Co Berthol; — Co strike out ׳ס not so Berthol Toy), compare 22:18 a. 19; indefinite Psa 119:119 .
